decisive_items: painless, non-erythematous, mobile, round mass (~2 cm) in the right parotid region
a few echogenic foci suggested debris
response.rationale: The clinical presentation of an elderly male smoker with a painless, mobile, well-circumscribed cystic parotid mass with echogenic debris strongly favors Warthin tumor. The FNA atypia and initial consideration of salivary duct carcinoma are recognized pitfalls, but the absence of aggressive features and the characteristic imaging make Warthin tumor the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.why: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma can be cystic but typically lacks the strong smoking association and well-circumscribed capsule; the imaging and clinical course are more consistent with Warthin tumor.
Pleomorphic adenoma is usually solid, not cystic, and would not explain the echogenic debris or the FNA findings.

Salivary duct carcinoma is an aggressive malignancy that would present with pain, fixation, or lymphadenopathy, which are absent; the well-circumscribed lesion with a thin capsule argues against this.
This is an append-only completion of R4 and inherits the same reasons for rejection; the diagnosis is not salivary duct carcinoma.
